616390260/daletou-predictor.body:
# Daletou Prediction Lab

The current experiments include a nine-model period-by-period comparison, an independent Laya review, and a [winning-coverage experiment](https://github.com/616390260/daletou-predictor/blob/HEAD/docs/PORTFOLIO.md) with a fixed nine bets totaling 18 yuan. Theoretical coverage, historical simulation, and results published before the actual draw are displayed separately; prizes and ROI are rule-based estimates.

[2026-10-16 retraining record](https://github.com/616390260/daletou-predictor/blob/HEAD/docs/RETRAINING_2026-10-16.md): LSTM, Transformer, and XGBoost have been fully retrained on corrected data through period 26117. The 60-period isolated validation has not yet outperformed the uniform-probability baseline.

A small experiment to **puncture the illusion that lottery can be predicted by algorithms**.

Five models with different approaches (random baseline, frequency statistics, Markov chain, LSTM neural network, genetic algorithm) predict Daletou numbers in parallel, generate 4 bets per draw, and after each draw compare long-term hit rates and return on investment against real results.

---

## Core ideas

- **Lottery is truly random**; any model's long-term hit rate should **converge to the random baseline**
- The point of this platform is **not "predicting winners"**, but:
  - verifying claims such as "hot and cold numbers", "number memory", and "neural networks can capture features"
  - providing a **fair long-term benchmark** so various "masters'" methods can be quantitatively tested
  - walking through the complete pipeline **data scraping → modeling → backtesting → visualization → automation**

## Architecture

```
data flow
  ├── China Sports Lottery official API
  ├── SQLite (data/daletou.db)
  ├── 5 prediction models
  └── export JSON → Vue3 frontend → GitHub Pages

scheduled tasks (GitHub Actions)
  ├── Mon/Wed/Sat 18:00 Beijing time → generate next-draw predictions
  └── Mon/Wed/Sat 22:30 Beijing time → fetch draw results + evaluate + redeploy frontend
```

## Directory structure

```
DaLeTou/
├── backend/                 # Python backend
│   ├── requirements.txt
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── config.py        # lottery rules / prize table / model list, etc.
│   │   ├── db/              # SQLite access
│   │   ├── scraper/         # historical data scraper
│   │   ├── models/          # 5 prediction models
│   │   ├── tasks/           # prediction / evaluation / backtesting
│   │   ├──…

Free Apple ID signing typically expires after 7 days. When the app won't open after expiration, reconnect the iPhone and press `Cmd + R` in Xcode to reinstall and renew the signing for 7 more days:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22
npx cap open ios

# CodeAgent-R

**Chinese** | [English](https://github.com/Phoenix-chaser/CodeAgent-R/blob/HEAD/README_EN.md)

An experimental post-training platform for code repair: public context construction → teacher candidate collection → test validation → data isolation → QLoRA SFT → paired base-and-adapter evaluation. A real single-GPU SFT and evaluation loop built on Hugging Face / PEFT is already in place; DPO and GRPO remain offline contracts and toy validation.

## Experiment results (v6, 2026-11-07)

| Set | Base | SFT | Change | Improved / regressed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dev (20 problems, used for model selection) | 10/20 (50%) | 12/20 (60%) | +10.0 pp, monotonic across epochs | +3 / −1 |
| **test (20 problems, frozen and unbiased, seed 42)** | **12/20 (60%)** | **13/20 (65%)** | **+5.0 pp** | **+1 / 0** |
| **test 3-seed summary** | 60% | — | **mean +1.7pp, CI [0, +5]** | **0 regressions** |

104 problems across 52 source groups (benchmark with mutation-testing audit of data quality), 202 replay-verified samples, QLoRA for 3 epochs, and checkpoints selected by dev execution pass@1 (Base included as a control). **Reproduced across 3 training seeds: mean +1.7pp (0/+5/0), zero regressions. When dev shows no gain, the selection mechanism automatically keeps the base model.** Full numbers, failure analysis, and honest limitations are in [v6 experiment results](https://github.com/Phoenix-chaser/CodeAgent-R/blob/HEAD/docs/EXPERIMENT-V6-RESULTS.md).

### Experiment evolution: every failed round has data pinning it down

| Round | Training samples | dev/test | Symptom | Root cause |

| v4 | 204 | 12/12 problems | dev +1 / test −1 | 12 problems dominated by noise; hidden tests incomplete |
| v5 | 60 | 12/12 problems | No change | One solution per problem cut supervised tokens to 26% |

chenming0v0/OMPiUI.body:
# OMPiUI

**Use the OMP programming assistant on your computer, phone, and browser.**

OMPiUI is a third-party client for [oh-my-pi (OMP)](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi). You can manage programming tasks on the desktop, or connect your phone to a computer or server to continue working on the same project.

The desktop app bundles the interface, the OMPiUI backend, and the official OMP runtime together. The mobile app only provides the interface, and tasks always run on the connected computer or server. Two terminal management interfaces are also available: one for managing headless backends, and one for managing a self-hosted public relay.

[Download and install](https://github.com/chenming0v0/OMPiUI/releases) · [Server deployment](https://github.com/chenming0v0/OMPiUI/blob/HEAD/deploy/README.md) · [Self-hosted relay](https://github.com/chenming0v0/OMPiUI/blob/HEAD/docs/tunnel.md) · [TUI usage guide](https://github.com/chenming0v0/OMPiUI/blob/HEAD/docs/tui.md)

## What you can do

- **Programming tasks**: chat, view tool execution results, use models and sub-agents, and access OMP's MCP, LSP, and extension capabilities.
- **Continue existing tasks**: shares native sessions with the official `omp`. Tasks started in the terminal and in OMPiUI can be opened and continued in either one.
- **Desktop use**: supports Windows, macOS, and Linux. The built-in backend starts automatically when the interface opens, and the title bar shows the local service status.
- **Phone connection**: the Android client supports scanning a QR code or pasting pairing information. The phone browser can also open the address shared by the backend directly.
- **Remote access**: connect to computers on an internal network using a LAN, your own public entry point, or a self-hosted relay.
- **Terminal management**: without a desktop environment, you can check status, start and stop services, adjust network settings, and manage relay tunnels.

## Choose how to use it

| What you want to do | Where to start |
| --- | --- |
| Program on your own computer | Download the desktop installer, configure models and credentials, then use the bundled official OMP |
| Connect your phone to a computer | Install the Android client, or open the address shared by the computer in your phone browser |
| Run tasks on a Linux server | Install the backend following the [headless deployment guide](https://github.com/chenming0v0/OMPiUI/blob/HEAD/deploy/README.md), then connect with your phone or browser |

# obsidian-cloud-attach

> An Obsidian plugin that connects to services such as OpenList via WebDAV, and to object storage (S3), so you can insert cloud files directly into notes. Frees up local space.

---

## Project Background

- A committed Obsidian vault user who keeps 0 attachments locally
- Heavy OpenList user
- Former e-commerce professional with zero coding background
- All work done with 🦞 Lobster

---

## Features

- 🌐 **WebDAV protocol** — Compatible with OpenList; in theory supports all WebDAV services such as Alist / Synology / QNAP
- 🌐 **S3 object storage** — Compatible with Cloudflare R2; in theory supports most object storage services such as AWS
- 📂 **Sidebar browsing** — Browse cloud directories directly in the Obsidian sidebar
- 📝 **One-click insert** — Single-click inserts a Markdown link; supports inserting one or multiple selections at once
- ⬆️ **Upload attachments** — Upload local attachments to the server and update references, saving local space
- 🔗 **Signed links** — Automatically generates URLs with a sign signature
- 🖼️ **Multimedia preview** — Image preview, video/audio playback, document iframe preview, **now supports online preview of HEIC format**
- 📄 **PDF.js preview** — In advanced settings, you can choose PDF.js as the preview tool, which is downloaded and applied automatically; when inserting a PDF, the `` syntax is used so it previews inline like an image
- 🎯 **Automatic attachment upload** — When enabled, attachments inserted into notes are automatically uploaded to the default service
- ⚙️ **Advanced settings** — Configure different preview methods for PDF and other formats; more formats (such as Office preview) will be supported later
- 👤 **Multi-account switching** — Manage multiple WebDAV/S3 accounts at the same time

---

## Installation

**Method 1: Download ZIP**

2. Unzip and place it in the `<vault>/.obsidian/plugins/cloud-attach/` directory

# ⚡ x-hub — Local Personal Productivity Workbench

A desktop productivity tool built with **Tauri 2 + Vue 3 + TypeScript**, featuring a Bento-style interface.
**All data is stored locally by default and is not uploaded to the cloud.**

## ✨ Features

### 🕐 Workbench
**Freely arranged Bento grid**: clock (**large clock / today's lunar-solar calendar / minimal time**, three display modes; quotes pulled from the online hitokoto service, falling back to a local corpus when offline), **weather card** (compact and detailed modes, real-time temperature / feels-like / humidity / wind speed from Open-Meteo, plus city/IP location), system resource monitor (CPU/memory, 2s polling), sticky notes ×2 (600ms debounced auto-save), **diary** (Enter saves to quick notes), **overview cards** for quick notes / to-dos / quick launch, prompt treasure box, to-do list, **to-do calendar** (monthly calendar marking to-do distribution and overdue items), countdown list, **custom quick launch ×4** (pin frequently used resources into groups for one-click launch), and a full-width recent-use strip. All widgets can be added, removed, dragged, resized, and switched between display modes in a **WYSIWYG layout editor**, and the layout can be saved as the default and restored at any time.

### ⏳ Countdown
**Four modes**: duration / scheduled / daily / interval (up to 6); pause / resume / floating window / delete; **background-driven** (Rust 1s polling, sends a system notification when due; `once` greyed out / `daily` / `interval` automatically reschedule; missed while asleep → silently rescheduled); can float out as a **transparent circular water-tank widget** (water-level wave animation, independent always-on-top small window, position persisted); optional alert sound when due (WebAudio-synthesized two-tone).

### 🚀 Quick Launch
Unified management of **three resource types**: apps / web pages / files; two-level filtering by **major category × minor category** and **custom sections** for grouped display; drag exe/lnk to import and **automatically extract high-resolution program icons** (native 256×256 extraction, including .lnk parsing); **scan installed apps for batch import**; one-click launch: **apps or browsers already running are brought to the foreground directly** (including minimized and tray-hidden windows), without opening a duplicate instance; web pages can be opened **in-app** (embedded panel in the main window or a standalone browser mini-window, multi-tab) or **in a specified browser**; usage notes + **encrypted notes** (encrypted locally on disk, peek-to-view with the eye icon); right-click menu actions; deletions can be undone.

kirayomato/vtb_dynamic_push.body:
# vtb_dynamic_push
## Introduction

Periodically checks specified Bilibili accounts for dynamic updates, livestream starts, and Weibo updates. If a change is detected, it sends a push notification.

This project is based on [nfe-w](https://github.com/nfe-w)'s [bili_dynamic_push](https://github.com/nfe-w/bili_dynamic_push) and [weibo_dynamic_push](https://github.com/nfe-w/weibo_dynamic_push/). Before using this project, it is recommended to read the introduction of the original projects.

This project adds several features on top of the original project:

1. Supports entering a Cookie to retrieve followers-only content, and notifies you when the Cookie becomes invalid

    The method for checking whether the Weibo Cookie is valid: if the fetched Weibo list contains followers-only Weibo posts, the Cookie is valid. You need an account that has recently posted followers-only Weibo content.

    Currently, Bilibili dynamics require a Cookie to be fetched; querying livestreams does not require one for now.

2. Windows pop-up notifications, more convenient for desktop users. The effect is shown below:

    

    Clicking the message or the button below opens the corresponding dynamic/livestream room link.

    Push notifications are implemented with the [win11toast](https://github.com/GitHub30/win11toast) library, which only supports **Windows10** and **Windows11**.

3. Weibo and dynamic detection adds detection of avatar and signature changes. Livestream detection adds detection of livestream room title and cover changes.

4. Monitors whether currently invisible Weibo posts have been published or deleted by detecting changes in the Weibo count. Supports detecting when users delete Weibo posts or dynamics. (Because the Weibo API may return erroneous data, results are not always accurate.)

5. For more features, see the configuration.

## Runtime Environment

- [Python 3](https://www.python.org/)

## Tutorial

#### 0. Download
Download the latest release archive from [Releases](https://github.com/kirayomato/vtb_dynamic_push/releases) and extract it into a folder.

#### 1. Fill in config.ini
First rename the file `config.ini.example` to `config.ini`, then fill in the parameters as follows.
Parameters under `scheduler`:
- `enable` whether to adjust the polling interval based on activity. When enabled, the polling interval is dynamically adjusted according to dynamic activity. The activity measure is the number of dynamics in the past seven days.
- `max_weight` maximum weight for a single ID. The polling interval is `sum(weights)/weight*intervals_second`

Parameters under `weibo`:
- `enable_dynamic_push` whether to enable Weibo push
- `uid_list` list of blogger UIDs to scan, separated by English commas

# verinote

A local web application that registers source texts, approves the entity, alias, and relation dictionary first, has humans review the wiki and relations extracted with that dictionary, and then queries only the approved knowledge through the actual Wirelog. It preserves document versions, exact citations, approval history, and query snapshots. Here, xAI means eXplainable AI.

## License

The source code of this project is distributed under the Mozilla Public License 2.0 (SPDX: `MPL-2.0`). For the full text, see [LICENSE](https://github.com/semantic-reasoning/verinote/blob/HEAD/LICENSE).

## Running

Python 3.11 or higher is required. To use a local CLI, that CLI must be installed and logged in. To use the OpenRouter API, a server key file and a model ID are required.

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e .
python -m verinote
```

Open <http://localhost:8765> in your browser. To change the data location and port, use `python -m verinote --data-dir /path/to/storage --port 8766`. The `verinote` command is equivalent. The program binds only to `127.0.0.1`.

### Server-only secret configuration file

Server credentials are stored in a TOML file, separate from the agent, model, and pricing settings in SQLite. On the settings screen, you choose one of the 5 local CLIs or **OpenRouter (API)** to run dictionary building, extraction, citation correction, and questions. The API does not require installing an executable. The default locations are as follows. On macOS, if neither location has a file, `--init-config` creates `~/Library/Application Support/verinote/config.toml`. If a file exists at the priority path, it is not replaced by another file even if it has empty key, format, or permission errors.

On Linux it also runs as a headless server (no desktop needed) that you use from a browser. The UI is Traditional Chinese with English and Simplified Chinese switches. timcsy/semorphe.description: Same program, three views: code, flowchart, and blocks. Edit any one and it counts, and all three stay in sync in real time!
timcsy/semorphe.body: Paste real C++ or Python code in, and it turns into blocks. Drag a block and the code changes along with it. Switch to the flowchart view and it draws the same program. 🔴 **All three sides are entry points, not "one editable plus two read-only"**: ``` You edit the code → blocks and flowchart update on the spot You edit the blocks → code and flowchart update on the spot You edit the flowchart → code and blocks update on the spot ``` There's no "convert" button, and nothing updates only on save. **While you type, the other two sides are already moving.** Type a piece of C++ → all three sides grow at once → edit once each in the code, the blocks, and the flowchart, and the other two sides update on the spot → press Run, and it really runs ## How it differs from other block tools Most block tools are **one-way**: blocks can become code, but code can't become blocks again. A few achieve two-way editing (for example MakeCode), but once you step outside the subset they support, you can't go back. Semorphe aims to do something else: | | | |---|---| | **All three views are editable, and live** | Edit **any** of code, flowchart, or blocks and the other two follow immediately. No "convert" button, and no updating only on save | | **Works with real code** | Paste in a `.cpp` or `.py` file you already have. It's not a toy subset | | **When it can't parse something, it says so** | Syntax it doesn't recognize is **neither dropped nor guessed**. It becomes a gray block with the original text kept verbatim inside | The third point doesn't sound like a selling point, but it is: **it guarantees the tool won't quietly break your file.** An unrecognized goto becomes a block showing the original text → change a number elsewhere → it doesn't touch a single character of it ## 🔴 The blocks live inside the Arduino IDE, not in another program This is Arduino IDE 2.3.8 itself. On the left is its own editor; the middle and right are **Tools that combine Arduino with blocks almost always live outside the Arduino IDE:** | Form | Examples | |---|---| | Another website | Tinkercad Circuits · Wokwi · Ardublockly | | Another desktop program | mBlock · S4A (Scratch for Arduino) | | A tool plugin for the IDE | ArduBlock (Arduino IDE 1.x, which still opens a **separate window**) | What they share is one thing: **the blocks are not in the editor you're already using.** So the workflow goes like this: assemble over there → export `.ino` → switch back to Arduino IDE → upload. And every "→" in that chain costs you something: ``` Two programs, two sets of files You have to remember which side you changed, and when you get it wrong, nobody tells you Uploading means switching windows Students' attention has to move house every single time Libraries / boards / serial ports… ```

wangshaojie/LibreTV-App.description: An unofficial cross-platform client based on LibreTV. The Windows portable edition and the Android app 静观 TV have both been released.
wangshaojie/LibreTV-App.body:
# 静观 TV

### Put LibreTV on your phone and TV: native clients, no installation, data stays on your device

[**Download Android APK**](https://github.com/wangshaojie/LibreTV-App/releases/download/android-v2.0.15/LibreTV-App-Android-v2.0.15-universal-android5.apk) · [**Download Windows portable edition (7z · 110 MB)**](https://github.com/wangshaojie/LibreTV-App/releases/download/v2.19.2-desktop.9/LibreTV-App-v2.19.2-desktop.9-Windows-x64.7z) · [**Windows ZIP · 159 MB**](https://github.com/wangshaojie/LibreTV-App/releases/download/v2.19.2-desktop.9/LibreTV-App-v2.19.2-desktop.9-Windows-x64.zip)

---

## What is this

**静观 TV** is an **unofficial cross-platform client** of [LibreSpark/LibreTV](https://github.com/LibreSpark/LibreTV).

The original is a web app that must be self-deployed with Docker. We turned it into two ready-to-use products:

- **Windows portable edition**: a green program directory plus a data directory. Extract and use, no need to install Node.js, Docker, or administrator rights.
- **Android native client**: a single APK with a native feel on both phone touchscreens and TV remotes. Supports older Android 5.0 TVs at minimum.

Includes **9 on-demand sources and 9 live sources** out of the box. Your source configuration, favorites, and watch history are **all stored on your own device**. No account, no telemetry, no ads.

## How it differs from the original

| | 静观 TV | Original LibreTV |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Android** | Native APK, phone touch + TV remote, minimum Android 5.0 | No official client |
| **Windows** | Green directory distribution, extract and use | Requires your own Docker deployment |
| **UI** | Same light theme on both platforms, custom-drawn dialogs | Web version |
| **Source updates** | Official manifest merged remotely; broken sources need no manual edits | Manually edit configuration |
| **Source health checks** | Batch liveness testing in both the Windows and Android native clients | Web version only |

wolforest/clean-rocketmq.description: Clean-RocketMQ is the fastest transactional messaging platform. 5x faster than RocketMQ.
wolforest/clean-rocketmq.body:
# Clean-RocketMQ **Clean-RocketMQ is the fastest transactional message queue.**
1. **Compatible with RocketMQ:** Can fully or partially replace RocketMQ. 2. **High performance:** Supports CommitLog sharding, with 5x+ RocketMQ throughput improvement. 3. **Transactional:** Supports distributed transactions (TCC), ensuring consistency of message sending and scheduling. 4. **More complete:** More complete support for delayed, expiring, periodic, cyclic and other message scheduling. 5. **Separation of storage and compute:** More reasonable splitting of the domain layer and storage layer, which is also the foundation of cloud native. 6. **CLEAN:** Introduces micro-framework and DDD thinking, easy to read and understand. > Clean-RocketMQ is the inheritance and optimization of RocketMQ.
> The RocketMQ core is less than 50,000 lines; it is not difficult to improve performance and extend features on its shoulders.
> The real challenge is:    **How to continuously keep the code clean and maintainable?** **Sibling projects:** * [RocketMQ-wolf](https://github.com/wolforest/rocketmq-wolf) : Refactored branch, production-ready, 100K+ optimizations, maintained for 1200+ days. * [RocketMQ-comment](https://github.com/wolforest/rocketmq-comment) : Official branch + pure annotated version. * [Clean-RocketMQ](https://github.com/wolforest/clean-rocketmq) : Rewritten from scratch, inheritance and evolution of RocketMQ. ## Project progress * [x] Core features (pub/sub, ordered/delayed messages, transactions, registry, RPC) * [x] CommitLog sharding * [ ] Master-slave architecture, separation of storage and compute (partially completed) * [ ] Richer scheduling and transaction features * [ ] Raft support, cloud native ## Software engineers in the AI era AI has arrived in full force, and it cannot be avoided. Fortunately, software is still software, whether handwritten or vibe-coded.
Software serves real business, and that remains the foundation of software engineers' livelihood, in the AI era as well. We have worked with RocketMQ for over 1200 days, and spent 400 days implementing Clean-RocketMQ from scratch.
We are ready to keep going for another 10, 20, or 35 years ... # Community In the AI era, embracing AI and continuous systematic learning are basic requirements for software engineers.
Communities are efficient learning accelerators. If you're interested, feel free to join us: * [RocketMQ study circle](https://wx.zsxq.com/group/28882125582281): Master RocketMQ thoroughly and grasp high concurrency. * [Software reading club](https://wx.zsxq.com/group/28851142528481): One book per week, from technology to capability. ###…

yalincc/BOTWmap.description: Breath of the Wild Botw Super All-in-One Interactive Map Navigation (supports Cemu\Ryujinx\Eden)
yalincc/BOTWmap.body:
# Breath of the Wild · Interactive Map

**[English](https://github.com/yalincc/BOTWmap/blob/HEAD/README_EN.md) | Simplified Chinese**

A multi-layer interactive map for The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild in Simplified Chinese · Collection progress tracking · Real-time character navigation

　

## What is this

A fully Chinese interactive map: all markers use the official Simplified Chinese names; multiple layers can be displayed at once, with collection progress tracking and custom markers. Optionally pair it with **xnavi** to show your character's position in real time while the game is running. It is a pure static page: open and use, with no server and no installation required.

## Direct use

| Method | Action |
|---|---|
| **Online version** | Open <https://botw.yalin.site/> |
| Local use | Open `app/index.html` in a browser (tiles, icons, and data are all local, so it works offline) |

Completion progress, layer selection, and custom markers are saved automatically in the browser, so they are not lost when the page is closed.

## Real-time character navigation (optional)

Want to see your current position on the map while playing? Pair it with **xnavi** (supports Cemu / Ryujinx / Eden on three platforms):

1. Launch the emulator and enter the game
2. Run `xnavi.exe` and click "Start positioning"
3. Open the online map; the real-time coordinates appear in the lower right corner
4. Phone/tablet following (optional): requires an offline local map. Download the map package `botwmap-vX.Y.Z.zip` (the `botwmap-vX.Y.Z` prefix in Releases), extract it into the same directory as `xnavi.exe` (merging with the navigation package), and scan the QR code in the GUI. See the README inside the xnavi archive for details.

- The three platforms are detected automatically, with no manual selection. It only reads memory; it does not inject into or modify the game.
- Save linkage: after the game saves, the map progress refreshes automatically within 2 seconds.
- For downloads and usage instructions, see [Releases](https://github.com/yalincc/BOTWmap/releases) (`xnavi-vX.Y.Z` prefix).

## Core features

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| Multi-layer display | Check any combination of marker layers; select all or clear with one click. Exploration/collection, facilities, enemies, and quests are four category groups, plus separate layers for equipment, treasure chests, camps, and materials |
| HD tiles | 7-level dynamic tiles loaded on demand. Still clear at up to 1:1 pixel ratio, with smooth dragging and zooming |
| Point details | Click any marker to see: Chinese name / category / region / tower domain / in-game coordinates / location hints |
| Search | Bilingual Chinese and English; search by region or tower name. Press Enter to jump directly, centering and zooming in |
| Collection tracking | Marking items complete automatically tallies completion across shrines / towers / divine beasts / Korok seeds / memories / treasure chests / quests. Save files can be uploaded for automatic sync |
| Material tracking | 74 types of materials / 13,524 gathering points, with a separate tab and dedicated search |
| Camp spawn points | 555…
